title: Ph.D. Project: Floorplan Quality Prediction for HLS Design Exploration on Multi-Die FPGA
problem: Cross multi-die boundary delays and local congestion in HLS designs on multi-die FPGAs require iterative parameter tuning through Vitis to achieve better frequency performance, consuming significant time overhead.
motivation: Accelerating design exploration is essential to reduce the massive time investment required for iterative FPGA tuning and enable faster development of optimized accelerators.
method: A graph neural network is trained to predict congestion (crowding of signals) and resource consumption for circuit layouts. Since predictions take milliseconds, designers can rapidly explore many layout options instead of iteratively running the slow Vitis design tool. This replaces manual parameter tuning with automated design space exploration.
key_novelty: A graph neural network trained to predict floorplan quality eliminates the need for expensive iterative Vitis design runs.
contributions: GNN-based floorplan quality predictor achieving 88.63% accuracy on high-level congestion prediction
Achieves 89.68% accuracy on critical resource prediction
Reduces design space exploration time from 7 hours to millisecond-level
Demonstrates 25% improvement in WNS performance compared to traditional tuning
